TAṂS, pour out (desires);
 cs. taṃsaya, P. shake.
2. TAN, Ⅳ. P. tanya, (v.) roar, resound.
3. tán, f. duration: in. continually.
tanayī-kṛta, pp. made a son.

tan-ikā, f. rope, cord;
 -i-tṛ, m. extender, 🞄performer.
tan-ū́, f., v. tan-ú.

tanū-karaṇa, n. attenuating;
 -kartṛ, m. diminisher.
tan-tí, f. (also ī) cord, rope (esp. for 🞄tying calves).
tāntra, n. (stringed) instrumental 🞄music.

tantra-ka, a. coming from the loom, 🞄quite new;
 —˚ a. doctrine, manual.
tantra-kāra, m. composer of a 🞄manual.
tantra-vāya, m. weaver.
tantr-in, m. soldier.
tantrillaka, m. N..

tan-trī, f. (nm. -s) string;
 music of a 🞄stringed instrument.
TAND, Ⅰ. Ā. tanda, relax, flag.
tandra-ya, den. Ā. grow weary.
tandrā-ya, den. Ā. grow weary.

tand-rā, f. lassitude;
 laziness, sloth.
tandrā-lu, a. weary, fatigued.

tan-nimitta, a. caused by him or 🞄thereby: -tva, n. being the cause thereof;
 🞄-niṣṭha, a. thoroughly devoted to that.

tan-ya-tú, m. roaring;
 thunder.

tanu‿aṅga, a. (ī) delicate-limbed, 🞄slenderly built;
 m. N..
tānvaṅga, m. pat. descendant of 🞄Tanvaṅga.
tanv-ī, f. (of tanu) slender maiden.

tānav-a, n. meagreness;
 smallness, 🞄slenderness: -kṛt, a. diminishing = surpassing 🞄(—˚).
tānūnaptr-a, n. ritual oath invocation 🞄of Tanūnapāt when the Ājya is 🞄touched by the sacrificer and the priests.

tāntrika, a. ā, ī completely versed 🞄in a system, specialist;
 taught in a Tantra.
